title: Preregistered Evidence Contracts: Disaggregating Implementation Delivery from Empirical Claim Corroboration
target_platform: Local Python runner; manage_backlog.py; deterministic test fixtures; bounded standard LLM review for claim decomposition
hypothesis: Adding a versioned evaluation contract to existing mission manifests (explicit claim IDs, numeric thresholds, evaluation scope, and cryptographic evidence references) will detect >= 95% of deliberately unsupported corroborations with <= 5% false rejection of supported results across 60 held-out evaluation cases, while deterministic validation adds < 500 ms p95 per mission excluding execution of the underlying experiment.
falsification_criteria: Detection falls below 95%, or false rejection exceeds 5%; any changed hypothesis can silently inherit evidence supporting its previous version; a partially supported result passes as full corroboration without explicitly narrowing and versioning the claim; or validation exceeds the < 500 ms p95 latency target. Unavailable evidence must be flagged unassessed, not automatically falsified.
experiment: Construct 20 valid cases, 20 invalid cases, and 20 partially supported cases (including missing evidence, failed thresholds, changed criteria, successful implementation with a failed hypothesis, and claims generalized beyond tested models). Compare current validation with the proposed contract using independently labeled expected results. Freeze the evaluation set before implementation.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: Escalate to bounded standard model (e.g. gpt-6-luna or claude-sonnet-5.5) solely for ambiguous natural-language claim decomposition into formal predicates.
